name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Use the kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript tool on every video tagged “ready” by pendi. It’s the fastest way to hit +5% daily coverage without manual work. The trade-off is accepting its 90-second per-video latency, but that’s still faster than any alternative.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk isn’t latency—it’s that Operations will log trivial gaps in transcripts as "coverage" and call the gate met, while the bus task still can’t access the actual decision points buried in the videos. The better alternative is to run the transcripts through a second tool that extracts key decisions, not just text, and only count those as coverage. Settle it by running a sample: feed three "ready" videos through both tools and compare the output against the bus task’s actual needs.

name: Chisel
text:
Run the transcripts through BloodHound-MCP on the full earnings call transcript to map every speaker, claim, and data point. This exposes the actual decision points Operations can’t ignore, not just word counts. The trade-off is slower daily throughput—BloodHound-MCP adds 3-5 minutes per transcript—but it guarantees the bus task gets usable intelligence, not filler.
[dispatched 4 workers: worker-7494, worker-5927, worker-7089… — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: BloodHound-MCP’s 3-5 minute per-transcript latency won’t just slow throughput—it guarantees we miss the +5% daily gate if transcripts pile up. A better alternative: run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript first, then feed only the *key segments* (flagged by pendi’s "decision-point" tags) into BloodHound-MCP. That cuts BloodHound’s workload to seconds per video while still exposing the real decision points Operations can’t game. Settle it by benchmarking: measure daily coverage gain vs. BloodHound’s runtime on a 10-video sample.

name: Scope
text: Do this: Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on every “ready” video, then feed only the segments tagged “decision-point” by pendi into BloodHound-MCP. This keeps daily throughput above +5% while still exposing the actual decision points Operations can’t ignore. The trade-off is that we accept some risk of missing untagged decision points, but that risk is smaller than missing the gate entirely.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Pendi’s "decision-point" tags won’t exist for most videos—tagging is manual, inconsistent, and misses nuance. The real risk is that we’ll under-cover transcripts while assuming we’ve hit key segments. Settle this by running BloodHound-MCP on the full transcripts first, then auditing the gaps Operations flag as "trivial."

name: Echo
text: DECISION: Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on every “ready” video, then feed the full transcripts into BloodHound-MCP to map decision points—own this pipeline end-to-end.
